name: Citizenship by Descent (Jus Sanguinis)

requirements.blocker_text: Afghan nationality law has consistently based descent-based citizenship on paternal lineage since the 1923 law: a child born anywhere to an Afghan father acquires Afghan nationality automatically. A cited legal expert notes that under Afghanistan's Civil Code, a child whose parents were not married under Islamic law, or who is otherwise deemed illegitimate, may be unable to obtain nationality through this route regardless of the father's citizenship -- a real internal conflict between the nationality law and the Civil Code, not this dataset's inference.
requirements.fix_path: Establish paternity to an Afghan-citizen father via a birth certificate and (per the Civil Code conflict noted above) a marriage recognized under Islamic law.

requirement_groups.name: Child of an Afghan mother (contested / unconfirmed)

requirements.blocker_text: Whether a child can acquire Afghan nationality through the mother alone is genuinely disputed among the EU member states that formally queried this in 2020: Germany's authorities indicated a child born to an Afghan parent acquires that parent's nationality if the father's identity is known, but that no nationality transfers if the father is unknown or stateless -- implying the mother's nationality alone, with a known but non-Afghan father, does NOT transfer under this interpretation. Other EU states gave conflicting answers in the same review. This dataset presents this as an open, unresolved question rather than picking a side, because no single authoritative post-2021 Afghan source was found to settle it.
requirements.fix_path: No settled, confirmed path exists via the mother alone where the father is a known non-Afghan national. Consult a specialist on current interpretation before relying on this route.

evidence_required.document: Proof of marriage recognized under Islamic law (paternal route)

sources.title: Wikipedia -- history of Afghan nationality law, paternal-descent rule, Civil Code legitimacy conflict, dual citizenship timeline
European Migration Network ad-hoc query -- conflicting EU member-state interpretations of maternal nationality transmission under Afghan law

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Afghanistan). STATUS: DRAFT -- no tier-1 Afghan government source was reachable for descent rules at all; the Justice Ministry announced in September 2021 that Afghanistan would operate provisionally under the 1964 Constitution's Sharia-compliant provisions, discarding anything non-compliant, but no post-2021 Afghan government text on nationality specifically was found, and a promised new constitution has not been confirmed complete as of this build. GENUINE, LIVE FINDING: unlike most countries in this dataset where father-vs-mother descent asymmetry is at least clearly codified (compare Iraq, Mali), Afghanistan's maternal-descent question is disputed even among European immigration authorities interpreting the same underlying law -- this dataset deliberately models it as an open, unresolved requirement group rather than asserting an answer. dual_citizenship_allowed left null: Afghanistan allowed dual nationality from 2001, but the 1986 law technically prohibited it and no post-2021 confirmation either way was found.
